items.stem: In scaled dot-product attention, a query happens to have exactly the same score with each of four keys. In one phrase, what is that query's output in terms of the four value vectors?
A team removes the division by the square root of d_k from attention in a model whose keys have d_k = 1024, and training stalls. Which explanation fits best?

options.text: The attention weights in each row stop summing to one
The scores shrink toward zero, so the weights become uniform
Large scores make softmax nearly one-hot, so gradients become tiny
The output vectors grow to 1024 times their usual length

items.stem: A decoder processes a sequence of 5 tokens with the standard causal mask in its self-attention. Counting token 3 itself, on how many tokens' value vectors can token 3's output depend? Give a number.
In one self-attention layer, the sequence length grows from n to 2n tokens while the key dimension stays the same. How does the number of entries in the score matrix QK^T change?

options.text: It doubles, growing in step with the sequence length
It quadruples, since every token scores every token
It stays the same, since it depends only on d_k
It grows eightfold, since it scales with the cube of n

items.stem: A transformer translates English into French. In its encoder-decoder attention, which sentence supplies the queries, English or French? Answer with the language and a reason in one sentence.
After softmax, one query's attention weights over three tokens are [0.5, 0.5, 0]. The tokens' value vectors are [2, 4], [6, 0] and [100, 100]. What is the query's output?
